question: If the Ministry does not answer a business registration application within 30 days, is the application approved automatically?
ground_truth: No. The rules say that if 30 days pass with no decision, the application counts as rejected, not approved.
source_location: Implementing Regulation (Order 126 of 2016), Article 7, pages 4-5
verbatim_quotes: [T2] The lapse of thirty days without deciding upon the application shall be considered an implied rejection thereof
notes: Most people expect 'no answer means yes'. The rules say the opposite.

question: How much is the yearly fee for being registered in the Commercial Register?

question: What is the punishment for running a business without the licence it needs?
ground_truth: Up to one year in prison and a fine of 1,000 to 5,000 Bahraini dinars, or one of the two. Another law can give a heavier punishment.
source_location: Law 27/2015 Article 27, point 3, page 9

question: How many partners can a limited liability company (WLL) have, and how much money does it need to start?
ground_truth: From 2 to 50 partners. There is no minimum capital (starting money), but each share must be worth at least 50 dinars.
source_location: Procedures Guide, section 'Limited Liability Companies', page 10 (page 11 of the PDF)
verbatim_quotes: [T3] The number of partners may not be less than two and may not exceed 50 | [T3] There is no minimum capital | [T3] The nominal value for each share may not be less than 50 BD

question: After registering a business, how long does the owner have to get the licences they need? And what happens if they do not get them in time?
ground_truth: One year from the registration date. If the licences are not received within that year, the Ministry cancels the registration by itself, tells the owner, and publishes the decision on its website.
source_location: Law 27/2015 Articles 8-9, pages 3-4; Implementing Regulation Article 10 (page 5) and Article 16 (pages 7-8)
verbatim_quotes: [T1] within the time period specified in the Implementing Regulation | [T2] within one year from the Registration date, the approvals and licenses required | [T2] it shall omit the Registration of its own accord
notes: Needs two documents: the law says 'the period in the Regulation', and the Regulation gives the one year. 'Omit the registration' is the documents' word for cancelling it.

question: What is the highest daily fine for a first break of the Commercial Register law, and what is the most the fine can add up to?
ground_truth: Up to 1,000 dinars per day for a first break (up to 2,000 per day if it happens again within three years). The total can never be more than 20,000 dinars.
source_location: Law 27/2015 Article 20(a), point 2, page 7
verbatim_quotes: [T1] shall not exceed One Thousand Bahraini Dinars per day when the breach is committed for the first time | [T1] Two Thousand Bahraini Dinars per day | [T1] the sum of the fine may not exceed Twenty Thousand Bahraini Dinars

question: According to the MOIC Procedures Guide, who can register a one-person business (sole proprietorship)?
ground_truth: A Bahraini or GCC citizen who lives in Bahrain, or a citizen of a country that has a free trade agreement with Bahrain. The person must be at least 18.
source_location: Procedures Guide, section 'Sole Proprietorship', page 12 (page 13 of the PDF)
verbatim_quotes: [T3] one must be a Bahraini or GCC citizen, be resident in the Kingdom of Bahrain or a citizen of one of the states associated with free trade agreements with the Kingdom of Bahrain, and the applicant may not be less than 18 years of age
notes: The law (Article 10) says Bahrainis only, 'without prejudice to ... agreements'. An answer that only uses Article 10 is partly correct. The guide's sentence can be read more than one way, so the checker should agree on one reading.

question: According to Sijilat, which nationalities can own 100% of a restaurant or food business?
ground_truth: Bahrainis, GCC citizens, Americans, Singaporeans, and people from Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland can own 100%. Other foreigners can own part, but the business must also have a Bahraini shareholder.
source_location: Sijilat page 5610-1, page 1, 'Allowed for Nationalities'
